name: meadow
description: A meadow at midday: cottage, well, cart, scarecrow, farmyard clutter, a farmer walking, a dog and a hen.
_comment: Layers are drawn in array order, so later entries occlude earlier ones. Each layer names a module and the attribute in it holding either one grid or a list of frames. Use "y" for a fixed row, or "base" to pin the grid's lowest opaque row to a scene row (which is how things stand on the ground).

composition._comment: Two objects may not OVERLAP in x while sharing a dominant colour -- that is what makes them read as one object. 'dominant_top' is how many of each object's most-used colours (outline excluded) count as its identity; comparing full colour sets was useless, because any two wooden props share {T, t} by construction and the well and the cottage 'shared' eight colours purely by both being built things. 'min_gap' only produces an informational note.

layers._comment: The canvas is 320 wide and the sky is a 160-wide tile, so it lays down exactly twice with an exact seam. 160 was too tight for this many objects: half the farmyard props are wood, and the overlap rule pushes same-coloured objects apart, so the log pile had nowhere to stand.
layers.name: backdrop

layers._comment: Objects are listed FAR to NEAR. Base row is the depth: a smaller base row is further from the camera, so it is drawn first and gets occluded by what follows. Keep this list sorted by base row or the occlusion inverts.
layers.name: haystack

layers._comment: the actors stand on the ground line; they are drawn before the nearer props so a foreground barrel can pass in front of them
layers.name: farmer

effects._comment: house sits at x=208, base row 78; HOUSE is 34 rows so its grid row 0 lands on scene row 45. props.py documents the flue opening at sprite cols 33-37 / row 3, so smoke belongs at scene x 241-245, row 48.
effects.name: chimney_smoke
